mentl/55408ea:
Four of verify.sh's legs ask one question — how many diagnostics of
class K did the judgment raise? — and each answered by grepping stderr,
re-deriving a count the diagnostics handler had already seen. So the
handler would tally per diag_code, board.mn would grow a BClass bound
beside its BShape ones, and four greps would die. It was built and it
worked: the tally kept located SITES rather than a count, Bound became a
two-variant sum with one Standing between them, and `mentl verify`
rendered 14 bounds, all holding.

The march killed it. m2 compiled clean; m3 died at exit 134 after 20,182
of 417,863 lines, judgment complete, no diagnostic anywhere. The stop
point named the cause without a probe: emit died generating
json_obj_get_loop, one of the two functions the T_EqTypeUnprovable
diagnostics name — the trap was in the report path.

The arm's own comment had said so before the edit: its projections are
pure ctor/string reads so the row carries no graph or intern demand and
the residual stays clean through every install; arms buffer, tally and
print, the line arrives made. The diag_report arm is deliberately
allocation-free because its residual rides every install, and an smap
tally performs Memory + Alloc. I read that comment while writing the
edit and added the allocation on top of it.

Ruled out: any accumulation in that arm allocates, so a growing
per-class tally cannot be handler state there. errors + 1 is fine
because an Int is not an allocation; named Int counters would be drift 8
in a gate's costume. Hβ.verify.class-bound-cannot-tally-in-the-arm.

Second finding, cheaper to state: two of the four bounds read 0 against
real ceilings of 4 and 60, because those classes are raised at
LOWER/EMIT and verify judges without emitting. A bound that reads zero
because nobody looked is worse than the grep it replaces — the same
vacuity this verb was caught by once before.
Hβ.verify.class-bounds-stop-at-the-judgment.

What landed is small and real: the anonymity ceiling

The canonical multi-shot effect substrate. `Choice` is the universal
"given these options, pick one" primitive every search problem
reaches for — N-queens, SAT, logic programming, parser combinators,
regex alternation, type inference's instance search, refinement-types
SMT goal direction. Per CE walkthrough §0.1: Choice is canonical
because it's universal; only the element type differs across
reach-for-it cases.

Substrate landings (one file, atomic):

- effect Choice { choose(options: List<A>) -> A @resume=MultiShot }
  Per QA Q-B.3.1 bare variant (NOT parameterized — Choice(Int) and
  Choice(String) are NOT distinct row entries; element type A flows).

- handler pick_first — OneShot terminal. Empty options → perform abort()
  per QA Q-B.3.2 (handler decides empty-list semantics). Useful as
  deterministic default OR capability-stack outer ("no more than one
  reality is explored at this boundary"). Resume discipline narrowing
  is implicit at install time; @resume=Either pattern would formalize
  in V2.

- fn try_with_abort_catch(try_fn, catch_fn) with Abort — small
  combinator backtrack uses to catch dead-ends. Composes on
  src/own.nx's catch_abort handler (which converts abort() into None).
  Per CE §1.3 + §4.0.2 halt-signal: substrate prerequisite for
  backtrack; ships in same commit (drift mode 9 deferred-by-omission
  avoided).

mentl/556c979:
The evidence dispatch now carries a bitmask encoding which state variables
were explicitly updated by the handler arm's resume. The VM only overwrites
those slots, preserving updates from nested dispatches on unchanged variables.

This fixes the re-entrant evidence dispatch bug that forced the revert to
pure function threading. Effect-based unification (subst_bind, subst_apply)
is restored in check.lux — push happens directly in handler arms where COW
can fire. The substitution flows through effects, not side channels.

Compiler: evidence body returns (resume_value, bitmask, state_0, ..., state_N).
VM: reads bitmask, only updates slots where bit is set.

perennials/55a4f07:
Every image in the guide was the full-resolution original -- a JPEG averaging
58 KB -- painted into a 56-pixel box. Permapeople's CDN is a plain S3 bucket
behind CloudFront with no image service, so `?width=` does nothing; the browser
was handed the whole photo and asked to guess. That is the guide's largest
ongoing cellular cost, and on a retina phone it is not even sharp.

The server now resizes with sharp and serves WebP at /img/<id>/<w>.webp, keyed
on the plant rather than a URL so it cannot become an open proxy, with the width
restricted to the four the layout actually asks for. srcset lets the phone pick:
a 3x screen wants 168 device pixels and gets the 192px file. A card thumbnail
drops from 58 KB to about 8 KB and is sharper than before.

Two things worth knowing about the source. Every photo Permapeople holds is
exactly 300px on its longest edge -- I sampled the CDN -- so the ladder stops
there; asking for more would return the same pixels under a bigger name. And the
detail photo was `width: 100%`, which on a desktop blew that 300px image up to
1,088px. No amount of processing fixes an upscale, so it is now mounted at its
true size on a tinted sheet, which is both sharp and closer to the herbarium
plate the design was always reaching for.
